items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] …Kenny Barron, Chico and Von, and Cecil McBee on bass. I just wanted to bring that up again because it goes back to the Chicago connection. [INTERVIEWEE] Was Wallace Roney on that?

ctx.x: Yeah, it was and it was formed again when I came back to Chicago and played Joe Segal’s Jazz Showcase. I had a band that was made up of Larry Gray on bass, a very fantastic bassist who plays with Ramsey. Larry Gray, the legendary Jodie Christian on piano, and Ira Sullivan. I did a week with Von Freeman with my quintet, which I have some documents of. That was great, playing with Von on a nightly basis. He had Ira and Jodie. It was fantastic. Anyway, the Fathers And Sons idea was for Columbia Records because of…
…Kenny Barron, Chico and Von, and Cecil McBee on bass. I just wanted to bring that up again because it goes back to the Chicago connection.
